lines: Project Meridian FACA 소송(11/2, D.C. 연방지법): CREW·Public Citizen·POGO 가 국방부·Hegseth·Michael 을 제소 — 머스크·Luckey·Gingrich 공동 디렉터 자문위(9/30 메모, 보고 기한 2027-01-28)가 헌장·공개 회의·균형 구성 없이 운영(21명 중 19명 민간). 청구는 메모 무효화·활동 금지·기록 공개. SpaceX 는 당사자 아님 · 8-K 없음 · 가처분 판정 없음 · 머스크 SGE 지위 미공개
닿는 경로는 둘뿐 — SGE 면 18 U.S.C. §208(SpaceX 이해 관련 사안 참여 금지) · 자문위 제언이 드론·우주 우선이면 E-2027-4(연방계약) 상방 배경. 둘 다 미확정 → 이정표 입력 아님. NPR: SpaceX 2026 국방 계약 $80억 초과(참고값). 축 E 에 '머스크 정부 역할' 이정표가 없다는 설계 공백 등재(월간 몫)
확률 25/50/25 · 가치 $32 · 이정표 29개 변화 없음(기준가 $141.31, 11/3 +3.6% → AI 내재가치 $1,377십억). T11(Meridian 소송 — 가처분·피고 답변·SGE·1/28 보고) 신설, 확인점 12/01 → 2027-01-29. T7 ⓓ·ⓔ·T8 ② 는 미국 11/3 기준 미도래. 10년물 4.91%(11/2)

새 분기 공시 없음(3Q26 유지) — 숫자의 상대방이 드러났다: 10-Q '고객 B'(3Q 매출 34.5%) = Anthropic(Bloomberg 10/29), 2029 년까지 최대 $1,205억·월 약 $31억·2027 초부터 90일 해지 가능(보도) → 상위 2개 고객 모두 2027-1H 해지 선택권. 규칙 신설 제안 ⑤ 등재, 확률 25/50/25 변화 없음

Fitch 10/28 BBB+ 불변 — $400억 리스는 1차 레버리지 지표 제외, 레버리지 2027 약 1.0배 전망(금리·체결 8-K 는 여전히 없음, T5 2027-01-07). 10월호 정정: 12/8 락업 '약 40%' → 424B4 원문 최대 7억 9,760만주(5.9%), 10/22 13억주 이미 해제, 2027 연장 락업 17억 6,000만주

scen.rationale: GW당 연매출 $150억 2개 분기 이상 유지 + 2027년 말 13GW 이상 명판 확인 + Ship 회수 성공
scen.label: Bull

scen.rationale: Starlink 성공하되 ARPU $50대 회귀, AI 는 2028~2029 갱신 구간 가격 하락으로 8GW 에서 증설 정체(GW당 $120억 가정)
scen.label: Base

scen.rationale: 고객 집중 51%의 상대방 이탈(Google 90일 해지 조항) + $400억 조달 8%대 고착 + Tesla 합병 희석 + Starship 재사용 미입증
scen.label: Bear

sections.html:
• Reference date: 2026-11-04 (KST) · run id 2026-11-04-event · mode event (incremental) · previous run 2026-11-03-event (run 9, event) · previous monthly run 2026-11 (Source: workflow-injected run info · _probe/context.json)
  • Reason: The news monitor detected one cluster of 2026-11-04 coverage and triggered the run — "Lawsuit Targets Secretive Musk-Led Pentagon Panel Over 'Enormous Potential Conflicts of Interest'" (common dreams · defense daily). Coverage not linked to any existing trigger (trigger_id: null) — the coverage is an item to verify, not a basis for judgment (Source: data/spacex_watch.json due news:pentagon-panel-lawsuit:2026-11-04, 2026-11-04 10:18 KST)
  • Reference price: $141.31 — 2026-11-03 (Tue) close, +3.62% from the previous day, volume 73.29 million shares. +3.6% versus the previous run's reference price of $136.37 (11/2) (formula: 141.31 ÷ 136.37 − 1) (stockanalysis daily history, retrieved 2026-11-04: latest row 11/3)
  • Scope: Only what the event touches — Axis E (Musk risk · federal contracts, background to milestone E-2027-4) and Axis C background (the Department of Defense's use of Grok). Trigger T11 newly created. Axes A, B and D, probabilities and fair-value recalculation are not performed (Source: prompts/monthly_run.md · state.triggers_next_12m).
Conclusion first: It is true — but SpaceX is not a party. On 2026-11-02 (Mon), three watchdog groups (CREW, Public Citizen, POGO) filed suit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia against the Department of Defense, Defense Secretary Hegseth and Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael. The defendants are government only, and the claim is that the advisory panel Hegseth established by a 9/30 memo, 'Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare', violated the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA — charter, balanced membership, open meetings, records disclosure), and the plaintiffs ask the court to void the memo, bar its activities until it complies with the law, disclose its records, and prevent action on its recommendations. Musk is a co-director of this panel (per the DoD announcement) along with Luckey (Anduril) and Gingrich, and the complaint states that 19 of the 21 members are civilians and that Musk and Luckey are "leaders and stakeholders of major defense contractors." No ruling on the merits or on a preliminary injunction (no reports of an injunction motion), the DoD and MITRE have not responded, and Musk's special government employee (SGE) status has been undisclosed since October. There is no SpaceX 8-K, IR or statement (latest EDGAR 8-K: 10/26). Therefore no change in the judgments on the 29 milestones · no rules triggered · probabilities 25/50/25 · probability-weighted $32 unchanged. What changed is one trigger (T11 — checkpoints for an injunction, the defendants' answer, SGE status and the 1/28 report) and the background facts of Axis E 'Musk risk'. The design gap that Axis E has no milestone measuring 'Musk's government role and conflicts of interest' is registered for the monthly run (Source: sections 1–5 below).

sections.title: 1 The Event — Press Reports vs. Original Text vs. Filings
sections.html:
Date (US)FactSource grade · source
2026-09-30Defense Secretary Hegseth announces Project Meridian in the Quantico 'State of the Force' speech + the same day a one-page (4-paragraph) memo "Commissioning of Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare" — directs Under Secretary for Research and Engineering and CTO Emil Michael to commission research 'through partner institutions.' Identify the future battlefield, required weapons and technologies; AI, autonomy, directed energy, robotics, biotechnology; from underground to cislunar space. Reporting deadline: 120 days after announcement = 2027-01-28, a declassified public report + a classified annex. The memo does not name Musk, Luckey or Gingrich — the designation of the three as co-directors appears in the speech and the Defense Department press release③ (government) memo PDF media.defense.gov · Defense Department press release war.gov 4615424 — both returned 403 to this round's tools; contents confirmed via ⑥ MIXED 10/02 (full summary of the memo) · The Next Web 09/30
2026-10-02Politico: the Defense Department held 2 meetings (attended by Senator Cotton and the Secretary's brother Phil Hegseth), 9 current and former officials warn of "conflicts of interest," SpaceX holds "2 multibillion-dollar contracts for a classified satellite constellation." Senators Kelly and Shaheen oppose⑥ Politico (Yahoo reprint) 10/02
2026-10-06NPR: SpaceX 2026 US defense contracts exceed $8 billion (tallied from government contract notices), operates Starshield, the Defense Department uses Grok. Defense Department spokesperson: "MITRE is responsible for analysis and recommendations, and conflict-of-interest and information-protection safeguards apply," time horizon 10–20 years. Whether Musk and Luckey are SGEs or contractors has not been disclosed — if SGEs, federal criminal law (bar on participating in decisions affecting one's own property interests) applies. Same day, Anduril Navy contract announced (up to $2.9 billion, submarine components — citing CNBC)⑤·⑥ NPR 10/06 (WFAE reprint) · NPR Illinois reprint · ⑥ OCBJ 10/06
2026-10-29POGO letter to the Defense Department — demands that budget expert William Hartung be seated as a member to provide balance, requests a reply by 10/30 (no reply)⑥ Military.com 11/03
2026-11-02 (Mon)Lawsuit filed — plaintiffs CREW, Public Citizen and POGO; defendants the Defense Department, Hegseth and Emil Michael; US District Court for the District of Columbia. Complaint is 37 pages (court PDF metadata creation 11/2 14:32 ET). Allegations: ① failure to meet FACA procedural and substantive requirements (no charter, closed meetings, unreleased records, unbalanced composition) ② by the MITRE roster, 3 co-directors + 17 participants, 19 of 21 are private citizens (the government side is only Michael and Air Force Chief Scientist Victoria Coleman) ③ Musk and Luckey are "leaders of and stakeholders in major defense contractors," and other members include Oracle (Catz), a Palantir co-founder (Lonsdale), Axon (Smith), Saronic, Hadrian, Agility Robotics, Stoke Space, etc. ④ no review of whether an existing chartered committee (the Science and Technology Innovation board) could do the work ⑤ the 9/30 (SCIF) and 10/1 (attended by Senators Cotton and Sheehy) meetings were closed ⑥ records requests unanswered. Relief sought: voiding the 9/30 memo · barring activity until FACA compliance · preserving and releasing records · barring acceptance or implementation of recommendations in the meantime. The complaint does not allege that "a particular member steered contracts." Filing alone does not halt the activity⑥ (plaintiff side) CREW · POGO (403 this round) · complaint PDF posted by Public Citizen · posted by CREW (redacted) — full text not read with this round's tools (cannot render); complaint contents cited from ⑥ Military.com 11/03 · Common Dreams 11/03 · Truthout 11/03 · Tampa Free Press 11/02
2026-11-03Defense Daily (paywalled — headline only): the complaint claims "the incentive grows for the Defense Department to steer contracts to member companies such as SpaceX and Anduril." The photo the Defense Department described as the 'first meeting of all members' was taken 10/1⑥ Defense Daily 11/03
2026-11-04 (KST)News watcher detection (Common Dreams · Defense Daily) — day 2 since filingdata/spacex_watch.json due
FilingsNo SpaceX 8-K, IR or statement (latest on EDGAR is the 10/26 8-K Item 8.01 GPU lease). SpaceX is not a defendant, and the legal proceedings note (R25) of the 10-Q (10/22) predates the filing and so does not include this case. Defense Department · MITRE: no response to requests for comment from Military.com and Common Dreams. Musk · Gingrich: no response to October Politico inquiries; Anduril issued a statement: "if an actual conflict of interest arises, we will comply with the highest ethical standards"① EDGAR filing list, accessed 2026-11-04 · 10-Q R25 · ⑥ reports above

Discrepancies between sources (recorded): ⓐ Number and order of meetings — Military.com (citing the complaint) "first SCIF gathering on the day of the 9/30 announcement + second meeting 10/1 (Cotton·Sheehy)" / Defense Daily "the Defense Department described the 10/1 photo as the 'first meeting of all members'" / Politico 10/2 "2 (Cotton·Phil Hegseth attended)" — reads as a difference over whether the 9/30 gathering counts as a 'meeting,' but unconfirmed since the complaint's text was not read ⓑ Anduril Navy contract — Common Dreams "$2 billion (CNBC 10/6)" vs OCBJ (citing CNBC) "up to $2.9 billion" — appears to be a difference in how the ceiling is stated, but the CNBC original (404) was not verified, number not adopted (unrelated to the SpaceX determination) ⓒ Number of members — the MITRE roster gives 3 + 17 = 20, while the complaint says '19 of 21 are private citizens' (reads as including Michael but unconfirmed) ⓓ Legal status of the co-directors — the memo has no names; they appear only in the Defense Department press release and speech — how the complaint characterizes the three as 'members' is unconfirmed as the original text was not read ⓔ Case number · assigned judge — not given in any report, CourtListener API 401, PACER not accessed (Source: table above · CourtListener API accessed 2026-11-04, 401).

Established as fact (3 plaintiff-side announcements + 4 cross-checked reports + government announcement): ① Filed 11/2 in D.D.C., 3 plaintiffs, defendants the Defense Department, Hegseth and Michael ② The claims are a declaration of FACA violation, voiding of the memo, barring of activity, and release of records ③ Project Meridian was established by the 9/30 memo with a reporting deadline of 2027-01-28 ④ Musk is a co-director per the Defense Department announcement ⑤ SpaceX is not a party. Unconfirmed: the complaint's original text (neither PDF could be rendered by the tools), case number · judge, whether a preliminary injunction was sought, Musk's SGE status, the full roster of all 21 members, the Defense Department's official response (Source: table above).

sections.title: 3 Proposal for new rules — none
sections.html: This case is not an input to the existing proposals ①–⑤, and the profit-and-loss path is not specific enough to establish a new rule (SpaceX is not a defendant). However, a design gap is noted: Axis E carries 'Musk risk' in name only and has no milestone — over the month of October, Musk's return to the Department of Defense advisory committee, the conflict-of-interest controversy and the lawsuit all passed outside any milestone. Whether to set a milestone such as 'zero events in which Musk's government role attaches conditions to SpaceX contracts through an official determination (a court FACA ruling, an OGE/Department of Defense ethics determination, or a congressional hearing)' will be decided by the monthly round (12/01) — event rounds cover increments only (source: state.rule_proposals_not_applied · state.axes · Section 1-1).
